description: The odd-channel Habiro datum is located in the bar-asymmetry of the cyclotomic coefficient C_{K,n}: C_n(q)f−C_n(q⁻¹)f = (C_n(q)−C_n(q⁻¹))f (f bar-even). 4₁ C_n=1 ⇒ zero odd datum; chiral C_n supplies it. 5₂ needs Masbaum's C_{5_2,n}. Lean: HabiroCyclotomicOddLocus. scope-(b).

assertions.name: odd_locus_identity
assertions.source: C(q)f(q)−C(q⁻¹)f(q⁻¹)=(C(q)−C(q⁻¹))·f(q) exactly, since the factor f is bar-even — the odd datum is the coefficient's bar-asymmetry (Lean: habiroTerm_bar_odd_eq_coeff_asymmetry)

assertions.name: fourone_bar_even_zero_odd
assertions.source: C_n=1 is bar-symmetric ⇒ zero bar-odd Habiro datum (bar-even tail; the #3970 π²/5 action is entirely bar-even)

assertions.name: chiral_coeff_gives_nonzero_odd_datum
assertions.source: a bar-asymmetric cyclotomic coefficient produces a nonzero bar-odd Habiro datum equal to (C_n(q)−C_n(q⁻¹))·f_n(q) — the odd channel is located in the coefficient asymmetry (demo with a toy C_n; the 5₂ coefficient is Masbaum's, to be derived)

result.verdict: LOCATED: the bar-odd (q↔q⁻¹ antisymmetric) content of any Kashaev/Habiro tail S_K(q)=Σ_n C_{K,n}(q)·f_n(q) is carried ENTIRELY by the cyclotomic coefficient's bar-asymmetry — C_n(q)f_n(q)−C_n(q⁻¹)f_n(q⁻¹) = (C_n(q)−C_n(q⁻¹))·f_n(q), since f_n is bar-even (Lean-proved). 4₁ has C_n=1 (bar-symmetric) ⇒ zero odd datum (bar-even tail, the π²/5 action all-even); a chiral knot's bar-asymmetric C_{K,n} supplies the odd datum. So the Q_β odd-channel resurgence (b3ix) lives in the cyclotomic-coefficient asymmetry — for 5₂ this is the Masbaum twist-knot coefficient C_{5_2,n}, the concrete next input (to be derived from that reference, not invented). scope-(b): a proved q↔q⁻¹ symmetry identity (Lean: HabiroCyclotomicOddLocus). NO fit; NO c_k wired.
